# Brake pad wear

## How I noticed

Sept 2024, a scraping squeal from the front left on light braking, coming down Gloucester Road. Not the high-pitched wear indicator, more of a grind. Pulled the wheel off on the drive that weekend.

## Measurements

Astra J front pads new are about 12mm of friction material. MOT fail limit is basically metal-on-metal but anything under 3mm is time.

| Position | Inner | Outer |
|---|---|---|
| Front left | 1.8mm | 3.9mm |
| Front right | 3.4mm | 4.1mm |
| Rear left | 5.2mm | 5.5mm |
| Rear right | 5.0mm | 5.4mm |

Inner front left much lower than outer = caliper slider pin sticking. Classic. Disc on that side had a lip of about 1.5mm and a blue tinge. Disc min thickness stamped on the hub side: 26mm. Measured 25.6mm. Bin.

## What got done

Had Stavros at Fishponds Autos do it because I didn't have a free weekend and wanted the slider pins done properly:
- Front discs and pads, Brembo, both sides
- New slider pin boots, pins cleaned and greased with red rubber grease
- Brake fluid change while he was there (it was 3.8% water on his tester)
- Invoice FA-2410-0388, 5 Oct 2024: £238 parts and labour, plus the oil change, see [[Oil change intervals]]
- Caliper carrier bolts torqued to 100 Nm + 45° + 15° (he showed me the angle gauge, Vauxhall do love a torque-to-angle)

## Bedding in

Stavros said: 10 moderate stops from 30 to 5 mph, no hard stops for 200 miles, don't sit with the brake on at the bottom of a hill when the discs are hot.

## Next check

Rear pads had at least another 15k in them. Checked again Mar 2025 at 119,700: rears 4.6mm. Pads were noted on the advisory list at the last MOT, see [[MOT failure notes]]. Brake light on the dash is a different story, see [[Dashboard warning lights]].
